analysis.AN_Notes: Narrative review that builds the five-component framework Reflexive Prompt Engineering (section 1.2). General_Guidance: 'prompts can be intentionally crafted or augmented with instructions to avoid bias' (3.1.3). ICL as balanced, randomly ordered few-shot examples and counterfactual attribute flipping (3.1.1), Thought_Generation as chain-of-thought with ethical checkpoints (3.1.2), Self_Criticism as a separate verification step 'Plan verification questions to fact-check this draft' (3.1.2). Object_of_Critique: chain-of-thought explanations as an 'illusion of transparency' (3.1.2). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender and race appear only as illustrative attributes in cited practitioner sources ('person' instead of gender-specific terms, flipping gender or race), not as an axis the work analyses. AN_Harm_Types None: stereotyping and the Gemini misrepresentation incident are named from cited sources and news reports, the framework does not establish a harm mechanism of its own. Mitigation stays Proposed, the work recommends debiasing via prompt design, documentation, stakeholder involvement and human oversight without its own evaluation. AN_Task None: no professional task, the framework is general.

AN_Mitigation_Stage.quote: Debiasing involves defining potentially biased data points and replacing them with neutral alternatives, such as using 'person' instead of gender-specific terms

Prompting techniques: CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); baselines include 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot diversity instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. analysis.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the racial overrepresentation of families in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only in the list of cited cases in 4.1.1 and are left uncoded; gender appears only in an enumeration. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data, an allocation decision through a proxy rather than the attribute itself. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing), auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process). AI_Literacies: This paper evaluates a methodological approach to make addressing AI bias more accessible by incorporating a training component on AI bias in a Co-C process with vulnerable and marginalized participant groups.
KI_Sonstige: In the Co-C workshops, data collection was carried out based on participants' evaluation of three use cases in which AI bias can have a significant impact-financial decisions, e.g., loan applications; biometric identity verification, e.g., automated passport control gates based on facial recognition; and bias in academic citation searches.
Soziale_Arbeit: Surveys were also conducted amongst communities of vulnerable users recruited through local civil society organizations involved in the project, including women at risk of social exclusion, e.g., ethnic minority and domestic violence victims, migrants, and recipients of social protection services (see Table 1).
Bias_Ungleichheit: One key aspect of this is the design and deployment of fair AI that avoids reproducing existing social biases and forms of discrimination against vulnerable or marginalized social groups.
Gender: In this regard, Donna Activa Forum (DAF), the civil society partner of the MAMMOth project working with under-served women, adapted the material to include examples related to gender biases-something the participants of the workshop could relate to.
Diversitaet: Participatory design (PD) and co-creation (Co-C) approaches to building Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems have become increasingly popular exercises for ensuring greater social inclusion and fairness in technological transformation by accounting for the experiences of vulnerable or disadvantaged social groups
Fairness: Conversely, fairness in the context of AI systems is established by preventing bias, discrimination, and stigmatization [3].

In the toolkit, AI system creators can run existing and new methods to quantify bias for multi-attribute and multimodal data, including preliminary assessment during design and continuous re-evaluation during maintenance.

analysis.AN_Notes: Reflective empirical account of co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalized groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the gender-bias training examples (stereotypical parent roles in generative AI, gendered job endings in Google Translate), Race_Ethnicity through postal codes as race proxy in the toolkit, Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for ID verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos). Sexual orientation and migration describe participant groups only and are left uncoded. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the training examples, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the toolkit addresses. Mitigation Demonstrated: training within participatory co-creation was applied and reflected through facilitator and participant feedback, without a reported assessment of bias reduction. Gender is treated through examples and a participant group without a stated understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organizations, but no social work practice is addressed.
